## Kyoto 6-Day Trip Plan: Temples, Markets, and Easy Transit
Media: Alt=Kyoto 6-Day Trip Plan: Temples, Markets, and Easy Transit, Kyoto, Japan

A comfortable pace for Kyoto is very doable on **JPY 180,000** for 2 travelers excluding flights, especially if you keep hotel choice moderate and group sights by neighborhood. This plan favors **short transit hops, low-walk temple visits, market stops, and one main outing per half-day**.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Budget Fit

### Day 1: Arrival, Gion, and Easy Evening Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and rest; keep the first day light.
- Afternoon: Explore **Gion** and **Yasaka Shrine** with a slow walk and tea break.
- Food: Dinner in **Pontocho** or near **Kawaramachi** for an easy first-night meal.
- Pace: Keep steps low; avoid adding a second temple today.
Media: Alt=Pace: Keep steps low; avoid adding a second temple today, Kyoto, Japan

### Day 2: Higashiyama Temples and Classic Kyoto Streets
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Visit **Kiyomizu-dera** early to beat crowds.
- Afternoon: Continue through **Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka** and finish with **Kodai-ji** or a nearby café stop.
- Food: Try **yudofu** or a simple Kyoto set lunch near Higashiyama.
- Pace: This is your main walking day, so keep the afternoon flexible and skip extra detours if tired.

### Day 3: Nishiki Market, Downtown, and a Short Temple Stop
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Morning: Browse **Nishiki Market** for snacks, sweets, and lunch bites.
Media: Alt=Morning: Browse **Nishiki Market** for snacks, sweets, and lunch bites, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Visit **Nijo Castle** or **Shoren-in** depending on energy.
- Food: Make lunch at the market; keep dinner casual near your hotel.
- Pace: Use this as a lower-pressure day after the more active Higashiyama outing.

### Day 4: Arashiyama Half-Day, Return Early
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Go to **Arashiyama** early for the bamboo grove and **Tenryu-ji**.
- Afternoon: Choose one easy add-on only: river area, monkey park only if everyone feels energetic, or a café break.
- Food: Lunch in Arashiyama, then return to central Kyoto before late afternoon.
- Pace: Do not stack too many sights here; Arashiyama can feel crowded and tiring.

### Day 5: Northern Kyoto Temples and Calm Neighborhood Time
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- Morning: Visit **Kinkaku-ji** early.
- Afternoon: Add **Ryoan-ji** or **Ninna-ji** only if you want a second temple; otherwise return to the hotel for rest and shopping.
- Food: Go for a relaxed dinner near **Kyoto Station** or your hotel area.
- Pace: Keep this day intentionally lighter to balance the trip.

### Day 6: Final Market Stop, Souvenirs, and Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/bag.svg
- Morning: Do a final short stop at **Nishiki Market** or a nearby shopping street.
- Afternoon: Pack, check out, and head to the airport or onward transport.
- Food: One easy lunch near transit so departure stays stress-free.
- Pace: Leave the last half-day mostly open in case of delays or shopping time.

## Spending Breakdown for JPY 180,000

| Category | Estimated Total | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hotel, 5 nights | JPY 85,000–110,000 | 2 beds, near transit, mid-range business hotel or compact city hotel |
| Food and drinks | JPY 35,000–45,000 | Mix of market snacks, casual lunches, and simple dinners |
| Local transport | JPY 10,000–16,000 | Subway, buses, and occasional taxi for convenience |
| Temple and attraction fees | JPY 6,000–10,000 | Mostly modest entry fees |
| Snacks, tea, souvenirs | JPY 12,000–20,000 | Keeps room for small purchases without overspending |
| Buffer | JPY 10,000–15,000 | Helpful for taxi rides, extra meals, or weather changes |

### Budget Takeaway
- A realistic target is **JPY 155,000–175,000** before extra shopping.
- If you want more comfort, prioritize spending on the **hotel location** and save by keeping lunches simple.
- If hotel pricing runs high, reduce souvenir spending first rather than cutting temple/food experiences.

## Sightseeing Pace That Avoids Overload

- Plan **1 major area per day**, not 3–4 scattered sights.
- Start early for the most popular temples, then use afternoons for markets, cafés, or a return to the hotel.
Media: Alt=Start early for the most popular temples, then use afternoons for markets, cafés, or a return to the hotel, Kyoto, Japan
- Build in **one lighter day after every active day**.
- Use taxis for short hops when it saves energy, especially between nearby but uphill temple areas.
- Keep one evening unscheduled so the trip never feels crowded.
- For your teen, add snack stops and short rest breaks every 2–3 hours.
